tagline: Oregon's highest road, up the long west slope of the Steens.
intro: Just past Frenchglen the loop road turns off Highway 205 and starts up the west slope of Steens Mountain, a single fault block some fifty miles long, built of more than forty lava flows stacked one on another. The road climbs to about 9,700 feet, the highest in Oregon, and nearly to the summit.

Along the way it reaches the overlooks above Kiger, Big Indian and Little Blitzen gorges, carved deep by glaciers. The fur traders called it the Snowy Mountains. In 1860 it took the name of an army major instead.

moments.title: Frenchglen
moments.text: Named for the French-Glenn Livestock Company, which built its headquarters here in 1872, the settlement is home to the 1917 Frenchglen Hotel, now a state heritage site.

moments.title: Whorehouse Meadow
moments.text: Women from Vale once pitched tents here for the sheepherders, and when the BLM maps changed the name to Naughty Girl Meadow, a public outcry put the old one back in 1981.

practical: Fuel, drinking water, restrooms and cell reception are all far apart on the mountain, and the BLM calls a current map essential.
